disclaimer: Independent investigation. Not auto-ingested into X-Ray scoring. Observed vs inferred labeled per claim.

findings.statement: Primary near-term binding constraint on leading NVIDIA-class AI accelerator shipments is advanced packaging allocation (CoWoS-class), not front-end logic wafer starts.
findings.why_matters: Lead times for packaging reported far longer than logic fab; industry analysis consistently places packaging as ceiling once HBM4 reaches multi-supplier volume.

sources.title: TSMC 3Q25 Earnings Call Transcript
sources.excerpt: CEO: AI-related frontend and backend capacity very tight; working to narrow CoWoS demand-supply gap into 2026.

sources.title: HBM4 volume shipping; CoWoS lead times stretch past 12 months
sources.excerpt: All three major HBM vendors in volume HBM4 for NVIDIA; qualification bottleneck shifted to packaging; CoWoS lead times >12 months.

findings.statement: HBM4 is no longer a single-supplier monopoly constraint: SK hynix, Micron (and Samsung) report volume/HVP paths in 2026, but qualified stack yield and allocation still matter.
findings.why_matters: Overturns simplistic 'HBM4 is THE bottleneck' if packaging is scarcer than qualified stacks; keeps HBM as co-constraint via yield/qualification.

sources.title: Micron HBM4 HVP for Vera Rubin
HBM4 capacity bottleneck analysis
sources.excerpt: Binding constraint framed as qualified shippable HBM / stacking yield, not raw wafer announcements.

findings.statement: Under CoWoS, the commercially meaningful deeper control layers are (a) large ABF package substrates + ABF film concentration and (b) installable bonding/assembly tool throughput — not only 'silicon interposer' as a standalone named node.
findings.why_matters: Fractal's 'advanced interposer' node may be mislabeled; organic ABF substrate / film may have more leverage and slower relief than interposer silicon.

sources.title: Ajinomoto Fine-Techno Gifu plant site for ABF
sources.excerpt: Construction 2028; operations 2032 — third ABF base after Kawasaki/Gunma.

sources.title: Ajinomoto Electronic Materials growth strategy
sources.excerpt: Gunma new plant entered operation 2025; staged capacity through 2030; Gifu for post-2030.

sources.title: Besi Q1 2026 earnings call (hybrid bonding capacity)
sources.excerpt: Hybrid bonder capacity expanded ~180→250 systems/year; ~6-month lead time; HBM needs far more bonders than logic (stack ratio).

findings.statement: Hybrid bonding equipment (esp. Besi) is a structural rate-limiter for NEXT-GEN HBM stacking densification and SoIC/CPO paths, but is NOT the primary reason today's CoWoS lines are sold out (current CoWoS still heavily microbump/TCB oriented).
findings.why_matters: Don't confuse current packaging bottleneck with future hybrid-bonding wall; Samsung large hybrid line install late 2026 targeting ~2029–2030 HVM.

findings.statement: Substitution exists technically (Intel EMIB-T, ASE FoCoS, Samsung I-Cube) but is NOT commercially equivalent for current NVIDIA flagship GPUs; useful mainly for ASIC spillover and 2027+ redesigns.
findings.why_matters: Supplier concentration at TSMC is overstated if counting all AI silicon, understated if counting NVIDIA GPU packages.

sources.title: Intel EMIB-T spillover amid CoWoS crunch

findings.statement: Ajinomoto ABF film capacity expansions are staged through 2030 with a third plant only operating ~2032; AI packages use more area and layers per unit, raising film intensity even if CoWoS tool counts rise.
findings.why_matters: Hidden missing Fractal node: ABF film / large organic substrate — small materials market, large downstream leverage; relief lag exceeds CoWoS fab announcements.

findings.statement: Contradiction: HBM remains tight on bits/pricing (2027 talks/pricing power) WHILE packaging lead times may still dominate system ship dates for GPU platforms — both can be true because they bind different parts of the chain.
findings.why_matters: X-Ray should allow co-binding constraints, not force a single winner.

findings.statement: CPO/silicon photonics is a real 2026–2027 networking scale path (NVIDIA Spectrum-X / Quantum-X) but is NOT a current GPU package production bottleneck.
findings.why_matters: Keeps CPO in model as next-wave interconnect constraint, not current accelerator ship limiter.
